ORIGINAL PHENOMENON CONTEXT:
An ideal capacitor and inductor form a closed circuit that exchanges stored electric and magnetic energy. Initial capacitor charge and loop current are selected independently, after which both quantities evolve together. The target is the instantaneous rate of change of current. The benchmark focuses on undamped electromagnetic energy exchange rather than resistive loss or external driving.

CURRENT EQUATION:
  dI_dt = -(Q + polarization_coupling*P_pol/(1 + (P_pol/polarization_saturation)**2) + slow_polarization_coupling*P_slow/(1 + (P_slow/slow_polarization_saturation)**2))/(capacitance*(1 + (Q/charge_saturation)**2)*(inductance*(1 + (I/current_saturation)**2)))

CURRENT SYMBOLS (symbol [role] — description):

  t [V] — time
  Q [S] — Charge stored on the selected capacitor plate in coulombs
  I [S] — Current around the circuit in amperes under a fixed sign convention
  P_pol [S] — Fast reversible internal dielectric polarization state contributing a lagged restoring charge-like term
  P_slow [S] — Slower reversible internal dielectric polarization state representing delayed bound-charge rearrangement | suggested range: Initial magnitude small but nonzero relative to slow_polarization_saturation and comparable to or smaller than P_pol so the slow memory branch is excited without dominating the capacitor charge.
  capacitance [P] — Small-signal capacitance scale in farads
  inductance [P] — Small-current inductance scale in henries
  charge_saturation [P] — Charge scale at which nonlinear capacitor saturation becomes appreciable
  current_saturation [P] — Current scale at which nonlinear inductive energy storage becomes appreciable
  polarization_relaxation_time [P] — Characteristic time for the fast internal polarization to relax toward the instantaneous charge-driven equilibrium
  polarization_coupling [P] — Strength with which the fast internal polarization contributes to the effective restoring charge
  polarization_saturation [P] — Polarization scale at which the fast restoring contribution saturates
  slow_polarization_relaxation_time [P] — Characteristic time for the slow polarization channel to relax toward the instantaneous charge-driven equilibrium | suggested range: Positive and typically several times polarization_relaxation_time, often comparable to or moderately larger than sqrt(inductance*capacitance) so the slow branch evolves within the observation window but remains distinct from the fast branch.
  slow_polarization_coupling [P] — Strength with which the slow polarization channel contributes to the effective restoring charge | suggested range: Positive, weak to order-unity relative to polarization_coupling so the slow branch measurably perturbs the restoring charge without overwhelming the primary capacitor term.
  slow_polarization_saturation [P] — Polarization scale at which the slow restoring contribution saturates | suggested range: Positive and comparable to or somewhat larger than the sampled |P_slow| range so both weakly nonlinear and saturated slow-polarization regimes can be observed.
